editorial.headline: Blank Media Manufacturing Is Nationally Open, But Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers the making of blank magnetic and optical recording media, nationally open to foreign ownership but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26800 is a manufacturing code for blank recording media: the physical carriers that can hold sound, images, or data before any content is placed on them. The record places audio and video magnetic tape, blank audio and video cassettes, blank vinyl records, unexposed film, data-recording tape, blank disks and diskettes, and blank optical discs inside the same industrial frame. Its center of gravity is not publishing, recording, duplication, or computer services; it is the making of the empty medium itself.

That distinction matters because this is a production activity, not a content activity. A company using this code is registering the industrial manufacture of carriers for future recording, storage, or distribution. The slim record opens the activity across the full business-size spectrum: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In practical registration language, the code is not reserved only for large factories in the national classification; the record says every listed scale is open to it.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is straightforward. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership figure in the record is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national layer alone, that means a foreign-owned company can treat the activity as open, with no lower foreign-share ceiling stated in the slim record. Nothing in the record adds a special national threshold, licence, timeline, capital rule, or operational condition, so none should be implied.

Bali changes the answer completely. The record marks this activity as blocked for PMA registration in Bali, with the Bali status Blocked (risk class). The stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule in the record is island-wide and permanent for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, and the cited source is Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. So the honest reading is narrow but decisive: KBLI 26800 is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, yet a foreign investor cannot register it as a PMA activity in Bali today under the Bali-side moratorium recorded here.
